title: Vasquez's latria fix: interior submission to God alone; images get only the exterior mark
source_text: LIX. Vasquez autem difficultatem istam aliter expedit, juxta posita ab ipso principia. Quamvis enim pertendat unico adorationis actu, imaginem cum exemplari coli, nec aliter esse colendam: in actu tamen illo, ut jam explicuimus, duas partes distinguit, unam quae est ipsa animi submissio, alteram quae est ejus submissionis signum. Et priorem illam partem, quae est animi submissio, non vult ullo modo respicere imaginem secundum se, atque ad eam terminari, sed referri ad solum exemplar: solam vero partem alteram, quae est submissionis nota quaedam exterior, imagini vult exhiberi, & per illam ad exemplar transire. Nempe cum aliquis coram imagine procumbit, aut genua flectit, id facit, ex ejus sententia, in signum servitutis atque reverentiae, quam deferendam putat, non imagini, sed prototypo soli. Jam vero latriae vocem significare vult, non notam exteriorem submissionis, & reverentiae secundum se, sed affectum subjectionis, ipsam vero notam prout subest, & perficitur interno servitutis affectu erga Deum. Unde colligit recte a Synodo Nicena secunda negari imaginibus deferendam esse latriam: quia, scilicet, illis non est exhibenda illa animae submissio, in qua latria proprie consistit.
pass_a_gloss: But Vasquez clears that difficulty otherwise, according to the principles laid down by him. For although he maintains that by a single act of adoration the image is cultivated with the exemplar, and is not otherwise to be cultivated: yet in that act, as we have already explained, he distinguishes two parts, one which is the very submission of mind, the other which is the sign of that submission. And that former part, which is the submission of mind, he does not wish in any way to regard the image according to itself and to be terminated in it, but to be referred to the exemplar alone: but only the other part, which is a certain exterior mark of submission, he wishes to be exhibited to the image, and through it to pass to the exemplar. Namely when someone prostrates before an image, or bends the knee, he does that, according to his opinion, in sign of servitude and reverence which he thinks ought to be deferred not to the image, but to the prototype alone. But he wishes the word latria to signify not the exterior mark of submission and reverence according to itself, but the affect of subjection, and the mark itself insofar as it underlies and is perfected by an internal affect of servitude toward God. Whence he gathers that it is rightly denied by the second Nicene Synod that latria is to be deferred to images: because, namely, that submission of soul in which latria properly consists is not to be exhibited to them.
pass_b_english: Vasquez's fix: one act, but split—interior submission aims only at the exemplar or God; the image gets only the exterior mark.
Latria names the interior servitude-affect toward God, not the bare gesture—so II Nicaea rightly denies latria to images.

choices.why: Cited as rightly denying latria to images on Vasquez's reading.
